tool.name: UMI isolation
tool.description: Extract UMIs, cluster their associated reads, and output a tabular file, a fasta file for BLAST and a zip archive.
tool.command:
set -euo pipefail &&
mkdir -p umi-work umi-cluster && python3 $__tool_directory__/umi-isolation.py -o '$output_tabular' -z umi-work/ -c umi-cluster/ -q '$output_fasta' -p $search_approach_options.process -f $input_files.input.single -l $additional_options.umi_length -s $search_method_options.search_method -a '$additional_options.forward' -b '$additional_options.reverse' -d $additional_options.identity_score -u $additional_options.abundance_score #if $input_files.input.single == "fastq" -i '$input_files.input.single_fastq' #elif $input_files.input.single == "fasta" -i '$input_files.input.single_fasta' #end if &&
## Keep only the original per-UMI read files for the zip archive. find umi-work -name 'derep*' -delete && find umi-work -name 'sorted*' -delete && (cd umi-work && python3 -m zipfile -c '$output_zip' .)

param.name: single
param.label: Input type
param.help: Select the input file format (default = FASTQ) [-f]

param.name: single_fastq
param.label: FASTQ file
param.help: Reads from which to extract UMIs [-i]

param.name: single_fasta
param.label: FASTA file
param.help: Reads from which to extract UMIs [-i]

param.name: process
param.label: UMI search approach
param.help: Search relative to a primer or scaffold (adapter), or from the first position (default = primer) [-p]. Expected read layout: [Forward_Scaffold(Adapter)]-[Forward_UMI]-[Forward_Primer]--READ--[Reverse_Primer]-[Reverse_UMI]-[Reverse_Scaffold(Adapter)]

param.name: search_method
param.label: UMI search method
param.help: Search for UMIs at the 5' end (umi5), the 3' end (umi3), or both ends (umidouble) of every read (default = umi5) [-s]

param.name: forward
param.label: 5'-end search nucleotides
param.help: The forward primer or scaffold (adapter) sequence to search for at the start of every read, in uppercase. N matches any nucleotide (default = NNNNNNNNNNNNNNN) [-a]

param.name: reverse
param.label: 3'-end search nucleotides
param.help: The reverse primer or scaffold (adapter) sequence to search for at the end of every read, in uppercase. N matches any nucleotide (default = NNNNNNNNNNNNNNN) [-b]

param.name: umi_length
param.label: UMI length
param.help: The number of bases in a single UMI (default = 0) [-l]

param.name: abundance_score
param.label: Minimum abundance
param.help: The minimum number of occurrences of a read required to retain it after dereplication (default = 1) [-u]

param.name: identity_score
param.label: Clustering identity
param.help: The minimum sequence identity for VSEARCH clustering within a UMI group, as a fraction from 0.1 to 1 (default = 0.97) [-d]

tool.help:
.. class:: infomark See VSEARCH documentation: https://github.com/torognes/vsearch for full software details.
**What it does** This tool reads a fastq or fasta file, extracts UMIs using the selected search settings, groups reads by UMI, and clusters each group with vsearch.
The tabular file contains the UMI identifier, UMI sequence, read count, and centroid read for each retained cluster.
The fasta file contains the centroid reads, ready for a separate BLAST search. The tool does not run BLAST itself.
The tool also creates a zip file containing the original per-UMI read files. It packages these files after clustering, but their contents are from before dereplication, abundance filtering, and clustering.
.. class:: warningmark Every read in a fasta file should have a header starting with >. Every read in a fastq file should have a header starting with @. Every read in a fasta/fastq file should be on one line. For instance, they cannot be "human readable" and have a "\\n" after every 80 characters.
